quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The phrase at the end tells you how long ago something happened.
quests.explanation: Nothing differs between what you read and what you heard. "A few minutes ago" places the call in the very recent past.
quests.prompt: She called me back a few minutes ago.
quests.sampleAnswer: She called me back a few minutes ago.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say something that happened a few minutes ago.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A day is named, and then a part of the day. Catch both.
quests.explanation: Morning and evening are far apart in a working day. Someone who waits at home would notice the difference straight away.
quests.prompt: The plumber is coming tomorrow morning.
quests.sampleAnswer: The plumber is coming tomorrow evening.
quests.followUpQuestion: Repeat the sentence and say the part of the day you heard.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two words together set the time. The second one is the one to check.
quests.explanation: Last year and last month both point to the past, but they are very different amounts of time.
quests.prompt: We moved to this flat last year.
quests.sampleAnswer: We moved to this flat last month.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say when you moved to where you live now.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Notice whether the visit is a habit or a single past event.
quests.explanation: A regular habit uses "visits" and "every". A one-time past event uses "visited" and "last". Both parts of the sentence carry the change.
quests.prompt: My cousin visits us every summer holiday.
quests.sampleAnswer: My cousin visited us last summer holiday.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say something a family member does every year.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A short word in the middle says the waiting has not ended.
quests.explanation: Same sentence on both sides. "Still" shows something has gone on for a while and continues now.
quests.prompt: I'm still waiting for the doctor's call.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm still waiting for the doctor's call.
quests.followUpQuestion: How would you say you're still waiting for something?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two ideas joined by "so". Follow both of them.
quests.explanation: The audio is faithful to the text. "Will" points to the future, and "soon" says it's close.
quests.prompt: The film will start soon, so please sit down.
quests.sampleAnswer: The film will start soon, so please sit down.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell someone to be quiet because a film is about to begin.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Listen for the word that says the action is finished.
quests.explanation: Exactly the same. "Already" tells us the departure is complete, perhaps earlier than expected.
quests.prompt: He has already left for the airport.
quests.sampleAnswer: He has already left for the airport.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say something you have already done today.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Listen to the ending of the verb near the start.
quests.explanation: "Opens" describes what happens now. "Opened" describes how it used to be. The ending of the verb carries the time.
quests.prompt: The bakery opens early on Sundays.
quests.sampleAnswer: The bakery opened early on Sundays.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say a place that opens early where you live.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence opens with a time phrase. Hold on to it while you listen.
quests.explanation: Both sentences begin the same way. Putting "next month" first is a common way to set the scene.
quests.prompt: Next month my sister starts her new job.
quests.sampleAnswer: Next month my sister starts her new job.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say one thing that will change for you next month.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Listen to the verb forms. Are they looking ahead or looking back?
quests.explanation: "I'll call" looks ahead and "I called" looks back. The pair "get" and "got" shifts the time in the same way.
quests.prompt: I'll call you when I get home.
quests.sampleAnswer: I called you when I got home.
quests.followUpQuestion: Promise to call a friend later.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence starts with the day and closes with a result.
quests.explanation: Word for word the same. "All afternoon" means the whole afternoon without a break, and "so" introduces what followed.
quests.prompt: Yesterday it rained all afternoon, so we stayed in.
quests.sampleAnswer: Yesterday it rained all afternoon, so we stayed in.
quests.followUpQuestion: How was the weather yesterday? Say it in a sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A negative statement about a schedule. Find the day.
quests.explanation: Weekends are easy to confuse when spoken fast. Sundays and Saturdays are different days, so the service is missing on another day.
quests.prompt: The bus doesn't run on Sundays.
quests.sampleAnswer: The bus doesn't run on Saturdays.
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask when the bus does run.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: There's a number, then a unit of time. Hear both.
quests.explanation: Two weeks and two days differ by a wide margin. You would plan your revision very differently.
quests.prompt: My exam is in two weeks.
quests.sampleAnswer: My exam is in two days.
quests.followUpQuestion: How long until your next big event?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Is the sending still to come, or is it already done?
quests.explanation: One sentence is a promise and the other is a completed action. "Later" and "earlier" also point in opposite time directions.
quests.prompt: I'll email you the photos later today.
quests.sampleAnswer: I emailed you the photos earlier today.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say when you will send a message to someone.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A reason follows the main idea. Listen to how the reason is introduced.
quests.explanation: You heard exactly what was written. "Because of" is followed by a noun, and here that noun is "the storm".
quests.prompt: We didn't go out because of the storm.
quests.sampleAnswer: We didn't go out because of the storm.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say why you stayed at home last time.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Tomorrow is the first word. What is the plan?
quests.explanation: The two sentences are the same. "I'm taking" is the usual form for a plan that is already arranged.
quests.prompt: Tomorrow I'm taking my son to football practice.
quests.sampleAnswer: Tomorrow I'm taking my son to football practice.
quests.followUpQuestion: What are you doing tomorrow? Use the -ing form.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: There's a contrast in the middle. Listen to what comes after "but".
quests.explanation: "Tomorrow" means the next day, and "later" means sometime today. The advice about when to go changes.
quests.prompt: The library is closed today, but it opens tomorrow.
quests.sampleAnswer: The library is closed today, but it opens later.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say when a place near you is open or closed.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two time periods are contrasted in one sentence.
quests.explanation: No differences at all. "Used to" describes a habit in the past that isn't true anymore, and "now" marks the change.
quests.prompt: I used to walk to school, but now I cycle.
quests.sampleAnswer: I used to walk to school, but now I cycle.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say something you used to do but don't do now.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The day is named, and then a moment of that day. Catch both.
quests.explanation: The meeting is on Wednesday in both cases, but morning and afternoon put it hours apart. People plan their whole day around this.
quests.prompt: The meeting was moved to Wednesday afternoon.
quests.sampleAnswer: The meeting was moved to Wednesday morning.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say the new time of a plan that has changed.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One small helping word gives you the time of the news.
quests.explanation: "Is feeling" describes now and "was feeling" describes an earlier moment. That single verb changes whether the report is current.
quests.prompt: My grandfather is feeling much better today.
quests.sampleAnswer: My grandfather was feeling much better today.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how you are feeling today.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This question checks whether something has been done. Listen for the word that suggests it.
quests.explanation: Audio and text are identical. "Already" in a question shows some surprise or a wish to check quickly.
quests.prompt: Have you already booked the hotel for July?
quests.sampleAnswer: Have you already booked the hotel for July?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a friend if they have already done something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: How many people? Listen to the ending of the noun and to the verb after it.
quests.explanation: Kids and kid, are and is, all shift together. Plural and singular subjects need matching verbs, so the difference appears twice.
quests.prompt: The kids are watching cartoons in the living room.
quests.sampleAnswer: The kid is watching cartoons in the living room.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say a sentence about how many people are in your room.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two events are linked in order. Which one waits for which?
quests.explanation: "As soon as" means immediately after, so the leaving depends on the rain stopping.
quests.prompt: As soon as the rain stops, we'll leave.
quests.sampleAnswer: As soon as the rain stops, we'll leave.
quests.followUpQuestion: Complete it: As soon as I finish work, I'll ...

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A period of time closes the sentence. Catch the number and the unit.
quests.explanation: The sentences agree. "Ago" counts backwards from now, so it always goes with the past.
quests.prompt: She started learning piano three years ago.
quests.sampleAnswer: She started learning piano three years ago.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how long ago you started something new.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Listen carefully to the ending of the verb near the middle.
quests.explanation: "Arrived" is finished and "arrives" is still to come. The small ending changes whether the parcel is already at the door.
quests.prompt: The parcel from my aunt arrived on Tuesday.
quests.sampleAnswer: The parcel from my aunt arrives on Tuesday.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what arrived at your house recently.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One small word near the end tells you who the person is.
quests.explanation: His and her point to different people. In a conversation, using the wrong one can confuse everyone.
quests.prompt: I still don't remember his name.
quests.sampleAnswer: I still don't remember her name.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say one thing you can't remember right now.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This is a plan or an expected event. When will it happen?
quests.explanation: Word for word the same. "Going to" shows something planned or expected, and "tomorrow" gives its time.
quests.prompt: They're going to announce the results tomorrow.
quests.sampleAnswer: They're going to announce the results tomorrow.
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask when the results will be ready.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A time phrase opens the sentence. Then follow what happened next.
quests.explanation: The audio and text are the same. Putting "after the concert" first lets you keep the order of events clear.
quests.prompt: After the concert, we walked home together.
quests.sampleAnswer: After the concert, we walked home together.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you did after your last meal.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Notice the reason. It is in the second half.
quests.explanation: Nothing is different here. "Because" gives the reason, and "was delayed" places the problem in the past.
quests.prompt: I'll be late because my train was delayed.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll be late because my train was delayed.
quests.followUpQuestion: How would you tell a friend you'll be late?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A duration ends the sentence. Compare the number carefully.
quests.explanation: Nine and six are different lengths of sleep. Numbers with hours are easy to mishear when there is background noise.
quests.prompt: Last night I slept for nine hours.
quests.sampleAnswer: Last night I slept for six hours.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how many hours you slept last night.
